claims.text: In eligible countries, the expanded Partner Program requires 500 subscribers and three valid public uploads in the preceding 90 days, plus either 3,000 qualified watch hours in 12 months or 3 million qualified Shorts views in 90 days.
claims.limitations: Program eligibility differs by country and feature; thresholds alone do not establish acceptance.

claims.text: Advertising and YouTube Premium revenue-sharing eligibility requires 1,000 subscribers with either 4,000 qualified watch hours in 12 months or 10 million qualified public Shorts views in 90 days.
claims.limitations: Channel review and additional requirements apply; thresholds are not guaranteed approval.

claims.text: Shorts Feed watch hours do not count toward the 4,000 qualifying public watch-hour threshold.
claims.limitations: Eligibility metric, not a statement about ordinary analytics watch time.

claims.text: Under the Watch Page Monetization Module, partners receive 55% of defined net revenue from eligible watch-page ads.
claims.limitations: The base is eligible net advertising revenue, not total advertiser spending or all video views.

claims.text: Under the Shorts Monetization Module, partners receive 45% of their allocation from the Shorts Creator Pool.
claims.limitations: Not 45% of gross ads alongside any single Short; music licensing and eligible engaged-view allocation matter.

claims.text: The Commerce Product Module provides 70% of defined net revenue for eligible fan-funding features including channel memberships and Supers.
claims.limitations: Net base, taxes, purchase channels and eligibility rules require separate consideration.

claims.text: Shorts Feed advertising revenue is allocated by qualified engaged views across monetizing creators in each country and subject to the Shorts pool allocation rules.
claims.limitations: This does not establish a fixed payout per Short or per view.

claims.text: YouTube's channel Analytics 'monthly audience' counts unique viewers over a rolling 28-day window.
claims.limitations: This is a creator's channel audience, not total unique users of YouTube.

claims.text: Age, gender and geographic reports may be limited, withheld or suppressed in YouTube Analytics for insufficient data or other platform restrictions.
claims.limitations: Absence of data is not evidence of zero users in any demographic category.

claims.text: The YouTube Analytics API documents ageGroup, gender and country as supported report dimensions for authorized analytics.
claims.limitations: Logged-in users and access-controlled channel data are not a platform-wide census; sex, ethnicity and political affiliation are not standard listed dimensions.

claims.text: YouTube Data API search.list reports approximate totalResults, not an exact census of matching people, communities or videos.
claims.limitations: Search and relevance sampling cannot establish unique users in a subculture.

claims.text: YouTube Data API channel statistics return subscriberCount rounded to three significant figures.
claims.limitations: Public channel subscriber values are approximate and subscribers may not be active viewers.

claims.text: YouTube Data API channel statistics expose a count of public uploaded videos, not a count of every video ever created.
claims.limitations: Private, unlisted or deleted content cannot be inferred from public counts.

claims.text: YouTube Analytics distinguishes views, engagedViews, watch time, estimated creator revenue, gross revenue and CPM-type metrics.
claims.limitations: The units and reporting basis differ by metric and report; estimated revenues may later be adjusted.

claims.text: YouTube requires creators to classify made-for-kids content using audience-directed factors; general-audience animation is not automatically made for kids.
claims.limitations: Classification depends on content and intent; age-directed legal rules vary by jurisdiction.

claims.text: Made-for-kids content has restrictions including personalized advertising and various social, community and commercial features.
claims.limitations: The exact effects differ for video versus channel settings and may change.

claims.text: YouTube's channel monetization policies require original, authentic content and address repetitive or mass-produced material.
claims.limitations: Content eligibility requires context-sensitive review; a genre alone does not imply monetization.

claims.text: YouTube distinguishes content that may receive full, limited or no advertising revenue under its advertiser-friendly guidelines.
claims.limitations: Per-video suitability can change and is context-dependent.

claims.text: Pew's 2026 survey found 84% of U.S. adults said they ever use YouTube.
claims.limitations: U.S. adults only; ever-use, not MAU, unique global users or monthly video views.

claims.text: DataReportal's Digital 2026 country reports give late-2025 estimated YouTube advertising reach of 85 million in Mexico, 254 million in the United States and 150 million in Brazil.
claims.limitations: These are advertising-planning estimates, not the platforms' monthly active users or deduplicated viewer counts.

claims.text: In a 2025 Pew survey, 92% of U.S. teens ages 13–17 reported ever using YouTube; the subgroup use rates were 94% among boys and 89% among girls.
claims.limitations: A U.S. teen sample distinct from the 2026 U.S. adult survey. These figures do not describe the demographic composition or children's content audiences.

insights.statement: YouTube Studio's monthly audience is a rolling 28-day unique-viewer metric for the creator's own channel, not the total platform user base.
insights.limitations: Cannot be aggregated across channels without a deduplication method.

insights.statement: Audience demographic breakdowns can be unavailable due to reporting thresholds and privacy restrictions.
insights.limitations: Do not infer missing categories or replace missing values with zero.

insights.statement: API search result totals are approximate and do not directly identify the number of unique people in a topic community.
insights.limitations: A representative audience-size study requires separate denominators, sampling or independently sourced surveys.

summary: YouTube combines video publication and discovery with advertising, subscriptions and creator payments. Primary-source research has begun on monetization eligibility, revenue formulas, audience measurement and policy limits. Platform population, subculture sizes and representative creator earnings are not yet established.
